summary: Cellular tether (phone hotspot) causes route/DNS precedence break -> internal artifact registries unreachable
description:
Issue summary: When engineers connect to corporate via WireGuard while also enabling a phone tether (iPhone or Android hotspot), some clients exhibit a change in route/DNS precedence that causes internal artifact registries (artifacts.redwood.internal) to fail name resolution or route to the public internet. Impact: Multiple engineers reported inability to download CI artifacts and docker layers; CI jobs started failing when builders were on shared tethering. Environment: macOS and Windows laptops using WireGuard client + split-tunnel policy (internal routes routed via wg0), phone hotspots on AT&T and T-Mobile. Intermittent across home and cafe hotspots.

Initial hypothesis: The tethered interface sometimes inserts a default route with higher metric or pushes DNS via captive portal, causing the OS resolver to prefer the cellular DNS or public route and bypass wg0. This results in DNS lookups for internal hostnames either failing or returning public addresses that are unroutable.

Business impact: CI failures for nightly and PR builds for some engineers, blocked deploys for small teams, increased support load.
steps_to_reproduce: Connect laptop to corporate WireGuard (wg0) with split-tunnel config that routes 10.0.0.0/8 and internal suffixes via wg0.
Enable phone hotspot (iPhone or Android) and connect the laptop to the tethered SSID.
On the laptop, confirm interface list (ipconfig / ifconfig) shows wg0 and the tether interface.
Attempt to resolve internal registry hostname: nslookup artifacts.redwood.internal
Attempt to curl a known internal artifact URL or docker pull from internal registry.
Toggle phone hotspot off/on and observe behavior changes (sometimes fixes until next tether).
observed_behavior: DNS resolves to public or fails; connections to artifacts.redwood.internal time out or route incorrectly. Sometimes TLS handshake fails because SNI/goes to public host. Behaviour is intermittent: works immediately after a fresh wg reconnect, breaks after hotspot reconnect or when mobile operator pushes DNS via captive portal.
expected_behavior: When wg0 is up and split-tunnel routes are configured, internal hostnames and routes should resolve and traverse wg0 regardless of tethered/mobile interfaces. No leakage to public DNS or default route should occur for internal prefixes.
logs: Mar 10 08:12:23 laptop-desktop wg0: peer xxxxx: handshake complete
Mar 10 08:12:31 Resolver: search list: redwood.internal local
Mar 10 08:12:38 DNS query artifacts.redwood.internal -> 8.8.4.4 (via tethered interface), NXDOMAIN
Mar 10 08:13:02 curl: (7) Failed to connect to artifacts.redwood.internal port 443: Operation timed out
Packet capture (tcpdump): SYN to 52.24.11.9 (public) from tether interface, no path to private range
investigation_notes: Support reproduced on macOS 13.5 and Windows 11 when using iPhone hotspot; behaviour differs by phone OS and mobile carrier.
Windows observed to prefer cellular adapter DNS when its metric is lower than wg0's resolver metric; macOS has resolver ordering quirks with SCPreferencesDomains.

WireGuard config shows allowed-ips includes 10.0.0.0/8 and search domain redwood.internal; client routing table contains correct routes but resolver lookup uses different resolver (OS-level behavior).
Tested workaround: setting wg0 interface metric lower (higher priority) and pinning system DNS to internal resolvers prevents leakage on some clients.
Hypothesis: Mobile operator/captive portal or phone DNS proxy is being pushed to the laptop via DHCP over tether; the client OS sometimes installs that DNS as system resolver ahead of wg0.
temporary_workarounds: 1) Reconnect WireGuard after enabling tether — immediate temporary fix in ~60% of cases.
2) On Windows: Increase priority/metric of wg0 adapter or add internal DNS server entries under adapter settings.
3) On macOS: use scutil to set resolver order for redwood.internal to use wg0 nameserver: 'sudo networksetup -setdnsservers <service> <internal-dns>' or create /etc/resolver/redwood.internal file.
4) Recommend engineers avoid phone tether for CI-critical runners until fix applied; use home router or dedicated mobile hotspot configured without operator DNS push.
resolution: In progress: Engineering networking team (Diego Martinez) to propose client-side guard rules and update WireGuard client configs to push DNS via a link-local resolver and use WG DNS handling (avoid OS-level DHCP DNS overrides).
Follow-up: Add platform docs for 'Hotspot + WireGuard' troubleshooting and per-OS steps (Confluence page linked).

Long-term: Scheduler to add CI runner affinity to skip builds triggered from tethered networks (policy), and evaluate bundling a small VPN client helper that enforces resolver priority across platforms.
If a specific engineer hits this frequently, escalate to IT for device-specific config or provide a USB-based workaround (Ethernet via phone) as stopgap.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) [2026-03-10]: Hit this in the morning — PR build failed in CI because docker pull timed out when on my phone hotspot. Attached tcpdump and nslookup output.
Support (Diego) [2026-03-10]: Reproduced. Collecting system-level resolver order and adapter metrics from affected machines. Can you confirm phone OS and carrier?
Aisha Patel [2026-03-10]: iPhone 15 Pro on AT&T. Also saw on Android Pixel 7 on T-Mobile for another engineer.

Network Eng (Diego) [2026-03-11]: Working hypothesis updated in investigation_notes. Will prototype a wg client change to prefer link-local DNS from wg0 and push change to the client-config repo. PR referenced above.

SRE (Marta Lopez) [2026-03-12]: Noting CI impact. Adding a temporary check in the runner that validates internal DNS resolution before pulling artifacts and fails fast with a descriptive error so engineers can switch networks.
